audits.title: Implementation of best practice for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in an acute care setting.
audits.standard: Four Joanna Briggs Institute best practice criteria
audits.setting: 33-bed oncology ward, large acute care hospital
audits.intervention: Audit-feedback-re-audit using JBI-PACES and GRiP to facilitate evidence-based nursing practice.

cycle2.result: All four criteria 100% compliance at second follow-up audit.

audits.other_findings: First post-implementation audit had all criteria >50% compliance.
audits.citation: Chung SK, Ahn MJ, Yoo JY, Choi M, Hyang N, Woo SR, et al.. Implementation of best practice for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in an acute care setting. Int J Evid Based Healthc. 2011;9(1):32-38. doi:10.1111/j.1744-1609.2010.00198.x. PMID: 21332661.

audits.title: An audit of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in children.
audits.standard: Anti-emetic prescribing proportional to emetogenic potential of chemotherapy (evidence-based practice)
audits.setting: National paediatric cancer unit, Our Lady's Children's Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Anti-emetic prescription was unrelated to the emetogenic potential of chemotherapy; dexamethasone was used in only 1 case; 20 children took no anti-emetics after discharge, of whom 11 had delayed vomiting.

audits.intervention: Evidence-based guidelines established with anti-emetic prescription proportional to emetogenic potential; education of staff, patients and families recommended. No re-audit reported.
audits.citation: Clinton F, Dowling M, Capra M. An audit of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in children. Nurs Child Young People. 2012;24(7):18-23. doi:10.7748/ncyp2012.09.24.7.18.c9274. PMID: 23155937.

audits.title: Increasing Olanzapine Prescribing for Patients Undergoing Highly Emetogenic Chemotherapy.
audits.standard: ASCO QOPI measure: olanzapine in 4-drug antiemetic regimen for first cycle of HEC
audits.setting: 38 Michigan Oncology Quality Consortium practices (71 sites)
audits.intervention: Audit and feedback with peer comparison, learning collaboratives, expert education, patient materials and value-based reimbursement from 2021.
audits.other_findings: Total of 8662 patients over 2019-2024; ongoing work targets practices with low rates.
audits.citation: Bowen AM, Cloud A, Fadly S, Gennette R, Hector-Word Z, Hirth J, et al.. Increasing Olanzapine Prescribing for Patients Undergoing Highly Emetogenic Chemotherapy. JAMA Netw Open. 2025;8(5):e2510392. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2025.10392. PMID: 40397444.

audits.title: A National Audit of Current UK Practice on the Use of Anti-Emetics for Chemotherapy-Induced Nausea and Vomiting in Children.
audits.setting: 12 UK paediatric oncology centres, inpatient episodes

cycle1.result: Concordance with guidelines 83%; emetogenicity overestimated in 6% and underestimated in 11%.

audits.other_findings: Authors suggest future audits include outpatient and ambulatory prescribing.
audits.citation: Neumann E, Jackson TJ, Morgan JE, Phillips R, Bate J, CCLG Supportive Care Group. A National Audit of Current UK Practice on the Use of Anti-Emetics for Chemotherapy-Induced Nausea and Vomiting in Children. Pediatr Blood Cancer. 2026;73(2):e70013. doi:10.1002/mpo.70013. PMID: 41267544.

audits.title: Improving the Appropriate Prescribing of Olanzapine for Chemotherapy-Induced Nausea and Vomiting: A Quality Improvement Initiative for the Outpatient Oncology Practice.
audits.standard: ASCO and NCCN antiemetic guidelines recommending olanzapine for highly emetogenic chemotherapy
audits.setting: Outpatient oncology clinic, Midwestern urban area (Karmanos Cancer Institute)
audits.intervention: Multidisciplinary interactive education for prescribers at monthly staff meetings on updated antiemetic guidelines, plus an olanzapine FAQ sheet (PDSA model).
audits.other_findings: Immediately after the intervention compliance was 94.74% (n = 76), a significant rise; the 2.15 point fall at one year was not significant.
audits.citation: Gennette RL, Dontje K, Rana J, Fadley S, Issawi E, Krupp R, et al.. Improving the Appropriate Prescribing of Olanzapine for Chemotherapy-Induced Nausea and Vomiting: A Quality Improvement Initiative for the Outpatient Oncology Practice. J Adv Pract Oncol. 2025. doi:10.6004/jadpro.2025.16.7.29. PMID: 41346771.

audits.title: Audit of guidelines for effective control of chemotherapy and radiotherapy induced emesis.
audits.standard: Audit criteria: 80% control with first courses; 85% control with subsequent courses; 90% lack of anticipatory nausea
audits.setting: Paediatric Oncology, Royal Hospital for Sick Children, Bristol

cycle1.result: Criteria met in two of three: 82% control for first courses, 83% for subsequent courses, 90% lack of anticipatory nausea.

audits.intervention: Minor modifications made to the guidelines after the audit (not re-audited)
audits.other_findings: The graded antiemetic guidelines were judged workable and acceptable.
audits.citation: Foot AB, Hayes C. Audit of guidelines for effective control of chemotherapy and radiotherapy induced emesis. Arch Dis Child. 1994;71(5):475-480. doi:10.1136/adc.71.5.475. PMID: 7826125.

audits.title: An audit of antiemetic use with CMF chemotherapy.

cycle1.result: Metoclopramide and dexamethasone policy: 9 of 21 patients (43%) switched for nausea or vomiting; emesis in 15 of 66 (23%) CMF cycles.

audits.intervention: Policy changed so that granisetron and dexamethasone were used for all patients.

cycle2.result: Granisetron and dexamethasone: 8 of 43 patients (19%) had emesis; emesis in 16 of 206 (8%) CMF cycles.

audits.other_findings: The abstract states the second stage involved 28 patients but reports 8 of 43; a lower granisetron dose (1 mg) was suggested to reduce cost.
audits.citation: Brown RS, Brown TK, Hoare D, Gaze MN. An audit of antiemetic use with CMF chemotherapy. Clin Oncol (R Coll Radiol). 1998;10(5):313-317. doi:10.1016/s0936-6555(98)80085-x. PMID: 9848332.
